oewn-15172673-n.learner: the part of a person's life after childhood and before they are fully grown up
examples: the greatest part of our youth was passed together
Wickham passed all his youth there, you know.

oewn-14449257-n.learner: the state of being young, or of being not yet fully grown, or of having little experience
examples: in spite of her youth and her manners, she retained all the claims to reputation which her marriage had given her

oewn-10824010-n.learner: a young person, most often a young man or a boy
examples: Such squeamish youths as cannot bear to be connected with a little absurdity are not worth a regret.

oewn-00059428-n.learner: the act of running away with the person you love, usually so that you can marry
examples: I joined them unexpectedly a day or two before the intended elopement
Had they no apprehension of anything before the elopement took place?

oewn-05758654-n.learner: the newest and most admired style in clothes, in make-up, and in how people behave
examples: His sisters were fine women, with an air of decided fashion.
He takes them now for people of fashion.

oewn-04936080-n.learner: the way in which something is done or the way it happens
examples: He told the whole story in a calm, careful fashion.

oewn-03328538-n.learner: goods that people buy, above all clothes, made in the style of the moment
examples: The shop windows were full of the season's new fashions.

oewn-02418610-v.learner: to put effort into something with your mind or your body, either to reach some aim or because you have to
examples: She worked hard all afternoon to finish the letter.
He works at his music every evening.
He works at the bank in town.
She has worked there since she left school.

oewn-01528454-v.learner: to do what it is meant to do when you use it
examples: The old clock still works.
The lock would not work until I oiled it.

oewn-00073433-r.learner: almost, but a little short of being done or reached
examples: The discussion of Mr. Collins's offer was now nearly at an end
her patience and her ideas were nearly worn out before the tête-à-tête was over
This question touches you more nearly than it touches me.

oewn-05646832-n.learner: a high skill that you can gain by studying, practising, and watching
examples: "And what arts did he use to separate them?"
Keeping a conversation going is an art you learn by practice.

oewn-00935235-n.learner: the making of things that are beautiful or that carry meaning
examples: The one was humanity, and the other was art.
He gave up medicine for art.

oewn-02746552-n.learner: the things people have made by being creative, thought of all together
examples: The gallery holds a fine collection of Italian art.
He seldom appeared really animated.
She seldom listened to anybody for more than half a minute

oewn-01830440-v.learner: to like one thing more than another, or to think it is worth more
examples: "Do you prefer reading to cards?"
I should infinitely prefer a book.

oewn-00681308-v.learner: to pick one thing instead of another one that was open to you
examples: found Elizabeth's arm inadequate to her support, and consequently preferred her husband's

oewn-02405179-v.learner: to push one person or thing forward ahead of another
examples: The colonel preferred his own nephew above officers who had served far longer.

oewn-04856472-n.learner: the quality of being morally very good, or of deserving to be admired
examples: all loveliness and goodness as she is!
One has got all the goodness, and the other all the appearance of it.

oewn-05149427-n.learner: whatever in something is pleasing, valuable, or useful
examples: Cook the vegetables lightly so that you keep the goodness in them.

oewn-06777755-n.learner: something you say that gives your own opinion or belief, or that adds a piece of information
examples: Lady Catherine continued her remarks on Elizabeth's performance
you ought to make some kind of remark on the size of the room

oewn-05718520-n.learner: open notice taken of something and said out loud
examples: The change in his manner was too great to escape remark.
